stageOrder: 0. fraction adjacency guard: a digit directly followed by a fraction character gets a space inserted (87½ -> 87 1/2) so the fraction conversion cannot read as a decimal
1. named substitutions (substitutions below; clinical micro multi-char rules first)
2a. transliteration fallback (fallbackTransliterations below; Latin letters that do not decompose under NFKD)
2b. NFKD decomposition: combining marks stripped; COMPATIBILITY characters fold (U+338D -> mu+g, circled digits -> digit, fullwidth -> ASCII) - this CHANGES content, it is not just mark-stripping
2c. post-NFKD micro re-application: the clinical micro rules (microSubstitutions below) run AGAIN over NFKD-produced mu sequences, so U+338D reads mcg - never mg (critic round-1 BLOCKER fix)
2d. Greek transliteration (greekTransliterations below; mu excluded - see the note)
6. final strip: anything still outside printable ASCII is REMOVED and surfaces as an unmapped-chars warning

knownOpenQuestion.behavior: CHARMAP maps standalone mu to "u" (the clinical micro convention), so a Greek word containing mu reads with u where the Greek m sound is. For dose text this is the SAFE direction; for Greek prose it is a documented approximation.
knownOpenQuestion.decision: CLINICIAN REVIEW at sign-off (trainingapp #357 AC2): keep, or add a context rule

removals.description: Characters NOT in the tables above that are removed: NFKD combining marks, C0/C1 control chars (kept: tab/newline/CR), and any remaining non-printable-ASCII character. Unmapped removals surface as warnings at run time.
